mission: Leave the internal JANUS registry as the evidence domain and independently verify the frozen Alan Parsons Project deep-mechanics claims against official artist pages, licensed sheet-music metadata, first-person Alan Parsons interviews, Abbey Road material and secondary music-theory sources.

source_policy.tier_1: Official The Alan Parsons Project site / Abbey Road / first-person Alan Parsons interviews
source_policy.tier_2: Licensed Musicnotes/Hal Leonard sheet-music metadata; reputable interviews/publications
source_policy.tier_3: Hooktheory and chord/transcription sites for harmony/key cross-checks only
source_policy.rule: Tier-3 evidence cannot silently override Tier-1/2 evidence. Unverified exact notes or production details remain unverified.

claim_matrix.subject: Eye in the Sky
claim_matrix.claim: Verse material centers B minor while chorus/pre-chorus shifts to relative D major.
evidence: Licensed Musicnotes metadata lists B minor as the original published key.
Hooktheory analyses verse/intro in B minor and pre-chorus/chorus in D major.
claim_matrix.note: In Russian theory terminology, B minor and D major are relative/parallel-associated keys sharing the same key signature; the transition claim is musically plausible and externally supported.

claim_matrix.subject: Eye in the Sky
claim_matrix.claim: Tempo is about 112 BPM.
evidence: Licensed Musicnotes arrangement metadata reports about 116 BPM; other analyses cluster near 112.
claim_matrix.claim_ceiling: Approximately 112-116 BPM depending on transcription/measurement; do not freeze 112 as uniquely authoritative.

claim_matrix.subject: Eye in the Sky
claim_matrix.claim: Exact simplified verse progression Bm -> G -> Bm -> G -> D -> A and chorus D -> F#m -> D -> F#m -> G -> A -> Bm -> G.
claim_matrix.evidence: External transcriptions support Bm/G/D/F#m as important harmonic material but show additional chords and section detail; the exact compact chains are not independently established as a complete authoritative transcription.

claim_matrix.subject: Eye in the Sky
claim_matrix.claim: Exact vocal-note sequence for 'I am the eye in the sky' is F# F# F# G F# E D.
claim_matrix.reason: The available licensed metadata establishes key/range but the exact seven-note sequence was not independently exposed in an authoritative accessible source during this pass. Preserve but do not promote.

claim_matrix.subject: Sirius -> Eye in the Sky
claim_matrix.claim: Sirius was intentionally keyed to function as the intro to Eye in the Sky and the two tracks form a continuous opening pair.
evidence: Official APP page lists Sirius first and Eye in the Sky second.
Alan Parsons states in the official expanded-edition notes that Sirius was later changed in key to make it an intro to the title track.
Licensed Musicnotes lists Sirius in B minor; Eye in the Sky is also published in B minor.

claim_matrix.subject: Sirius
claim_matrix.claim: Core pulse is exactly the three-note B-D-F# arpeggio and Eye vocal begins from the same three-note DNA.
claim_matrix.reason: Shared key and intentional intro linkage are verified, but this exact reduction was not independently established in the accessible authoritative sources.

claim_matrix.subject: Sirius
claim_matrix.claim: Fairlight is central to the track's programmed basis.
evidence: Official APP credits: Fairlight — Alan Parsons.
Alan Parsons states in a first-person interview that Fairlight Page R sequencing was the basis for Sirius, using a Fairlight-sampled clavinet.

claim_matrix.subject: Don't Answer Me
claim_matrix.claim: The production deliberately emulates Phil Spector's Wall of Sound.
evidence: Alan Parsons explicitly describes it as a deliberate attempt to emulate the Phil Spector sound.
Expanded-edition notes describe Eric Woolfson's desire to recreate the Wall of Sound and the layering/reverb process.

claim_matrix.subject: Don't Answer Me
claim_matrix.claim: Original key is B-flat major with a B-flat -> Gm -> E-flat -> F I-vi-IV-V cycle.
claim_matrix.correction: Licensed Musicnotes metadata lists C major as the original published key. Common transcriptions begin C -> Am -> Dm -> G, which is I-vi-ii-V, not I-vi-IV-V.

claim_matrix.subject: Don't Answer Me
claim_matrix.claim: Mel Collins plays the saxophone solo.

claim_matrix.subject: Don't Answer Me
claim_matrix.claim: The animated clip concept/animation was created by Michael Patterson.
claim_matrix.correction: The clip is associated with comic-book artist Michael/Mike Kaluta and Broadcast Arts. Michael Patterson is not supported as the creator of this APP video in the checked evidence.

claim_matrix.subject: Don't Answer Me
claim_matrix.claim: Exactly three or four acoustic guitars and equivalent fixed overdub counts were used.
claim_matrix.evidence: Official credits confirm electric and acoustic guitars and expanded notes confirm many layers of overdubs, but the exact three-or-four count was not verified.

claim_matrix.subject: I Robot
claim_matrix.claim: The title track uses an EMS Synthi-A sequencer/programming and human choral/vocal elements.
claim_matrix.evidence: Official APP credits list Projectron & Synthi-A Sequencer Programming by Alan Parsons, soprano Hilary Western, The English Chorale, and live band instrumentation.

claim_matrix.subject: I Robot
claim_matrix.claim: The electronic machine layer literally absorbs/subordinates the human choir by the ending.
claim_matrix.reason: The machine/human contrast is a defensible listening interpretation, but the checked sources do not establish it as literal authorial production intent.

claim_matrix.subject: In the Lap of the Gods
claim_matrix.claim: The track begins from harpsichord and the choir is wordless.
claim_matrix.correction: Official credits list Middle Eastern wooden flute, cimbalom, piano and organ, acoustic guitars, rhythm section, English Chorale and orchestra; no harpsichord is credited. Alan Parsons also explicitly discusses a choral section with sung words, so 'wordless choir' is not sustainable as a blanket claim.

claim_matrix.subject: In the Lap of the Gods
claim_matrix.claim: The choral melody ascends chromatically by semitones and then drops in a specific architectural pattern.
claim_matrix.reason: Instrumentation and choral/orchestral construction are verified; exact interval-by-interval geometry was not independently verified in this pass.

claim_matrix.subject: Lucifer
claim_matrix.claim: The track is in C minor with a repeated C bass pulse and a C-Eb-F-G-Bb-C pentatonic main theme.
claim_matrix.correction: Licensed Musicnotes lists D minor as the original published key; Hooktheory analyses D Dorian; chord analyses also center D minor. The claimed C-minor center is not supported.

claim_matrix.subject: Lucifer
claim_matrix.claim: The main theme is played on clavinet through wah-wah.
claim_matrix.correction: Official Lucifer credits list autoharp, drum machine and FX compilation (Alan Parsons), synths (Duncan Mackay), guitars (Ian Bairnson and Alan Parsons), bass, drums, orchestra and choir. Clavinet is credited on the next track, You Lie Down With Dogs; backwards wah-wah is credited on I'd Rather Be A Man, not Lucifer.

claim_matrix.subject: Ammonia Avenue
claim_matrix.claim: The title/image came from Eric Woolfson's visit to the ICI chemical plant and a pipe-lined road called Ammonia Avenue; the album concerns science/industry versus public understanding.

claim_matrix.subject: Ammonia Avenue
claim_matrix.claim: The title track is in E minor.
claim_matrix.evidence: Independent transcriptions center the original recording around B-flat/A-sharp minor rather than E minor. Official APP credits do not publish a key, so the correction remains transcription-derived rather than Tier-1.

claim_matrix.subject: Ammonia Avenue
claim_matrix.claim: Christopher Rainbow plays a saxophone solo that hands the melody to Ian Bairnson's guitar.
claim_matrix.correction: Official title-track credits list Chris Rainbow on backing vocals, Ian Bairnson on electric/acoustic/Spanish guitars, and the Philharmonia Orchestra arranged/conducted by Andrew Powell. No saxophone is credited on the title track.

claim_matrix.subject: Analog studio method
claim_matrix.claim: Double tracking with small varispeed offsets is a characteristic Alan Parsons technique, especially on fixed-pitch instruments/guitars.
evidence: Parsons describes double track with varispeed as a concept used on his records and a trademark-like sound.
In a first-person Q&A he confirms Eye in the Sky lead vocal was double-tracked and says varispeed double-tracking is especially magical on acoustic/electric guitars.

claim_matrix.subject: Analog studio method
claim_matrix.claim: Abbey Road used physical echo chambers where a speaker played the source and microphones recaptured the room response.
claim_matrix.boundary: This verifies the chamber method at Abbey Road, not that every APP track cited in the user analysis used that chamber in the exact described way.

claim_matrix.subject: Pink Floyd - Time
claim_matrix.claim: Alan Parsons recorded individual clocks separately in an antique/clock shop before Dark Side and proposed using them for Time.

claim_matrix.subject: Pink Floyd - Time
claim_matrix.claim: The clocks were assembled as many physical tape loops held by people/pencils around the studio and started simultaneously.
claim_matrix.correction: Parsons' first-person accounts describe each clock recorded separately and then combined/aligned on multitrack. The checked sources do not support the pencil-held multiple-loop story for Time.

claim_matrix.subject: Pink Floyd - Money
claim_matrix.claim: A seven-beat sound-effects tape loop was physically assembled, measured with a ruler, recorded to multitrack, and the band played to it without a separate click.

claim_matrix.subject: Pink Floyd - Money
claim_matrix.claim: Exactly 7.5 inches of tape equals each quarter note and every loop segment was that fixed length.
claim_matrix.correction: Parsons supports ruler-based precise measurement, but first-person accounts describe multiple sound pieces and one account gives varying segment lengths around 6, 7 and 8 inches. The fixed 7.5-inch rule should not be retained as fact.

hard_or_substantial_passes: Sirius intentionally changed in key to lead into Eye in the Sky
Eye in the Sky B-minor/D-major sectional relationship broadly supported
Don't Answer Me deliberate Wall of Sound homage
Mel Collins sax solo on Don't Answer Me
I Robot Synthi-A sequencer plus human choir
In the Lap of the Gods verified orchestral/choral/cimbalom/flute instrumentation
Abbey Road physical echo chamber method
Time individual clock recordings and Parsons contribution
Money seven-beat measured tape loop used as performance timing reference
major_corrections: Don't Answer Me is C major in licensed original-published-key metadata, not B-flat major.
Don't Answer Me's simple opening is C-Am-Dm-G (I-vi-ii-V) in common transcriptions, not the claimed I-vi-IV-V chain.
Don't Answer Me video art/animation points to Mike Kaluta/Broadcast Arts, not Michael Patterson.
In the Lap of the Gods does not have a credited harpsichord and its choir is not simply wordless.
Lucifer is not supported as C minor; licensed sheet metadata says D minor and Hooktheory says D Dorian.
Lucifer's clavinet/wah claim is misattributed to other Eve tracks.
Ammonia Avenue title track has no credited sax; Chris Rainbow is backing vocals, not saxophonist.
Ammonia Avenue E-minor claim is not supported by checked transcriptions.
Time pencil-held multi-loop story was not verified.
Money fixed 7.5-inch segment claim was not verified and conflicts with varying-length first-person recollection.
open_claims: Exact Eye in the Sky seven-note vocal sequence
Exact B-D-F# three-note Sirius DNA reduction
Exact interval/chromatic ascent geometry in In the Lap of the Gods
Exact fixed overdub counts on Don't Answer Me
summary.strongest_world_result: The external check validates several structural/production foundations but also breaks multiple attractive technical details. The JANUS difference-operator analogy survives at the level of verified production contrast and continuity; several note-level and instrument-level claims must be corrected or left open.

canonical_seal: THE WORLD CONFIRMED THE BRIDGE AND BROKE SOME DECORATIONS. KEEP BOTH. SIRIUS REALLY WAS RETUNED TO LEAD INTO THE EYE; WALL OF SOUND, SYNTHI-A, INDUSTRIAL AMMONIA, CLOCKS AND THE MONEY LOOP SURVIVE. B-FLAT DON'T ANSWER ME, C-MINOR LUCIFER, THE LUCIFER CLAVINET-WAH, THE AMMONIA SAX RELAY, WORDLESS GODS CHOIR, AND THE FIXED 7.5-INCH MONEY RULE DO NOT SURVIVE AS STATED.
